title: Crispy Hasselback Potatoes
summary: Whole potatoes are thinly sliced almost all the way through, basted with butter and herbs, and roasted until the fanned slices turn crisp and golden. It's a simple way to get far more crunchy, buttery surface than a regular roast potato.
equipment: baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: medium floury or all-purpose potatoes (about 150 g each), scrubbed
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead so the potatoes start crisping as soon as they go in.

steps.title: Slice the potatoes
steps.text: Lay a potato between two chopsticks and cut straight down across it at 3mm intervals, stopping when the knife meets the chopsticks so the base stays whole. The chopsticks act as a guide and a stop, keeping every potato fanned but intact.

steps.title: Rinse and dry
steps.text: Rinse each potato under cold water, gently fanning the slices apart to wash away loose starch, then dry thoroughly. A dry surface is essential for the fat to crisp the slices rather than steam them.

steps.title: Baste and season
steps.text: Mix the melted butter, oil, salt, pepper and chopped herbs in a small bowl, then brush generously over and between the slices.

steps.title: First roast
steps.text: Roast for 30 minutes, by which time the slices will have started to fan open and turn pale gold at the edges.

steps.title: Baste again
steps.text: Brush the potatoes again with the fat from the tray, easing the slices apart slightly so the baste reaches deeper between them.

steps.title: Finish roasting
steps.text: Roast for a further 30-40 minutes, basting every 15-20 minutes with the fat in the tray, until the edges are crisp and golden and a skewer slides easily into the centre. As the slices open further during roasting, each basting reaches further down between them, so the whole potato crisps evenly.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with flaky sea salt and serve while the edges are still crackling.

tips: Cut almost all the way through but stop at the chopsticks — cutting too far will separate the slices completely instead of leaving a fanned potato.
Dry the potatoes thoroughly after rinsing; any leftover water on the surface will steam instead of crisp in the oven.
Baste more than once during roasting — a single basting at the start is the most common reason the lower slices stay pale and soft.
Choose potatoes of a similar size so they all roast through in the same time.
storage: Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot oven at 200°C (180°C fan) for 10-15 minutes until piping hot and crisp again, rather than microwaving, which will soften the edges. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
